title: Technical MCQ Set 04: Concurrency, Algorithms & Spring/SQL
description: Covers Java functional interfaces, equals/compareTo consistency, SQL EXISTS vs JOIN, Dijkstra vs Bellman-Ford, OS disk/paging, and ARP/NAT.

questions.question: What happens when you try to compile and run the following Java snippet?
options: Prints `2 4 6`
Prints `3 6 9`
Compilation error: local variable `factor` referenced from a lambda expression must be final or effectively final
Throws `UnsupportedOperationException` at runtime
questions.explanation: Lambdas capture local variables by value, so Java requires any captured local variable to be `final` or effectively final (never reassigned).

questions.question: A `Task` implements `Comparable<Task>` comparing only `priority`. `t1 = new Task("A", 1)` and `t2 = new Task("B", 1)`. Both are added to a `TreeSet<Task>`. What is `set.size()`?
options: `1` (only `t1` is retained)
`2` (both `t1` and `t2` are stored)
Throws `ClassCastException`
questions.explanation: `TreeSet` determines key equality using `compareTo()` (returning `0`), NOT `equals()`. Because `t1.compareTo(t2) == 0`, `TreeSet` treats `t2` as a duplicate and keeps `set.size() == 1`.

questions.question: What is the exact output of this Java snippet?
questions.explanation: In `a > 3 || ++b > 10`, `a > 3` is true, so `||` short-circuits and `++b` does NOT run (`b` stays 10). In the inner `if`, `a > 10` is false, so `&&` short-circuits and `++b` again does NOT run. Output: `5:10`.

questions.question: When should you implement `Comparator<T>` rather than `Comparable<T>`?
options: When you want to define multiple independent sort orders (e.g., sort by salary, then by name) or sort a third-party class you cannot edit
Only when sorting primitive `int[]` arrays
Whenever you need `HashMap` bucket hashing
`Comparator` is only used in Java 7 and removed in Java 8
questions.explanation: `Comparable` defines one natural ordering inside the class itself (`compareTo`), whereas `Comparator` enables external, multiple custom orderings (`compare`).

questions.question: In `try (ResourceA a = new ResourceA(); ResourceB b = new ResourceB()) { ... }`, in what order are `close()` methods called?
options: `a.close()` then `b.close()`
`b.close()` then `a.close()` (reverse declaration order)
Simultaneously on daemon threads
Only `b.close()` is called unless an exception occurs
questions.explanation: Java's `try-with-resources` closes resources in the exact reverse order of their declaration (`b` then `a`), ensuring outer/dependent resources close before underlying connections.

questions.question: Why does modern OOP favor Composition ('has-a') over deep Inheritance ('is-a') hierarchies?
options: Inheritance is unsupported for generic classes in Java
Composition preserves encapsulation, avoids fragile base-class coupling, and allows swapping behaviors dynamically at runtime
Composition eliminates the need for interfaces
Inherited methods cannot be unit-tested with JUnit
questions.explanation: Inheriting implementation tightly couples subclasses to parent internals (fragile base class), whereas composition delegates to interfaces that can be swapped or mocked cleanly at runtime.

questions.question: Why does `SELECT dept_id, emp_name, MAX(salary) FROM Employees GROUP BY dept_id;` fail in strict ANSI SQL / PostgreSQL?
options: `MAX()` cannot be combined with `GROUP BY`
`emp_name` is neither included in `GROUP BY` nor wrapped in an aggregate function
`dept_id` must also appear inside `HAVING`
SQL forbids selecting more than two columns with `GROUP BY`
questions.explanation: Every non-aggregated expression in the `SELECT` list must be functionally dependent on or listed in `GROUP BY`; otherwise SQL cannot deterministically pick which `emp_name` represents the group.

questions.question: When checking whether at least one matching order exists per customer, why is `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders o WHERE o.cust_id = c.id)` often faster than `IN` or an unaggregated `JOIN`?
options: `EXISTS` skips creating any query execution plan
`EXISTS` short-circuits as soon as the first matching row is found (semi-join) and handles NULLs safely
`EXISTS` caches results permanently in browser cookies
`EXISTS` disables table locks on `Orders`
questions.explanation: `EXISTS` uses a semi-join that stops scanning for a customer on the very first matching order row and never fails on NULL subqueries like `NOT IN`.

questions.question: Why do relational databases overwhelmingly use B+Trees rather than plain B-Trees for table indexes?
options: B+Trees allow O(1) unsorted point lookups without comparisons
B+Trees keep internal nodes compact (keys only, higher branching factor) and link leaf nodes sequentially for fast range scans
B+Trees never require node splitting during inserts
B+Trees store records exclusively in RAM rather than disk blocks
questions.explanation: Omitting data pointers from internal nodes lets B+Trees pack far more keys per disk page (shallower tree), while doubly-linked leaf pages make `BETWEEN` / `ORDER BY` range scans sequential.

questions.question: A relation `R(A, B, C, D)` has a single candidate key `{A, B}`. How many distinct SUPERKEYS does `R` have?
questions.explanation: Any superkey must contain `{A, B}`, and each of the remaining 2 attributes (`C`, `D`) may independently be included or excluded: 2^2 = 4 superkeys (`AB`, `ABC`, `ABD`, `ABCD`).

questions.subtopic: FIFO vs LRU Page Faults Numerical
questions.question: For page reference string `1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 5, 1, 2, 3` with 3 empty page frames, how many page faults occur under LRU?
If each process in memory spends 80% of its time waiting for I/O (`p = 0.8`), approximately what is the CPU utilization when 3 such independent processes are in memory?
questions.explanation: Probability all 3 processes wait for I/O simultaneously = `p^n = 0.8^3 = 0.512`. Therefore CPU utilization = `1 - 0.512 = 0.488 = 48.8%`.

questions.question: How does a home/office router running NAPT (PAT) allow 50 devices with private IPs (`192.168.1.x`) to share a single public IPv4 address simultaneously?
options: By broadcasting all packets to every host on the internet
By rewriting the source IP to the router's public IP and mapping unique source TCP/UDP port numbers in a NAT translation table
By assigning each laptop a temporary IPv6 MAC address
By encapsulating HTTP inside ICMP ping replies
questions.explanation: PAT (Port Address Translation) maps `(privateIP, privatePort)` <-> `(publicIP, uniqueMappedPort)` so returning packets can be demultiplexed back to the exact internal host.

questions.question: An organization owns a `/22` IPv4 block and splits it equally into subnets supporting at least 120 usable hosts each. What is the maximum number of such equal subnets it can create?
questions.explanation: Supporting >= 120 usable hosts requires `2^h - 2 >= 120` => `h = 7` host bits (126 usable hosts, `/25` prefix). Splitting `/22` into `/25` borrows `25 - 22 = 3` subnet bits => `2^3 = 8` subnets.

questions.question: Why does standard Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm fail on graphs containing negative edge weights?
options: Priority queues cannot store negative integers
Dijkstra greedily marks the popped vertex's distance as final, assuming adding future edges cannot decrease path cost
Dijkstra requires the graph to be a DAG
Dijkstra runs in exponential time on negative edges
questions.explanation: Dijkstra assumes non-negative weights guarantee monotonically non-decreasing path lengths; a later negative edge could yield a shorter path to an already settled vertex. Use Bellman-Ford instead.

questions.question: Which pair of traversals is sufficient to reconstruct a general Binary Tree (with distinct keys) UNIQUELY?
options: Preorder and Postorder only
Inorder and Preorder (or Inorder and Postorder)
Level-order and Preorder only
Postorder alone
questions.explanation: Preorder/Postorder identifies the root, while Inorder partitions nodes into left vs right subtrees. Without Inorder, single-child subtrees remain ambiguous.

questions.question: In Spring Boot, why does calling a `@Transactional` method `saveOrder()` from another method `placeOrder()` inside the SAME bean class fail to start a transaction?
options: Spring proxies only intercept `static` methods
Self-invocation (`this.saveOrder()`) bypasses the Spring AOP proxy wrapper around the bean
`@Transactional` only works on `@RestController` classes
Checked exceptions always commit transactions automatically
questions.explanation: Spring AOP creates a proxy around the bean; external callers go through the proxy, whereas internal `this.method()` calls bypass the proxy completely.

questions.question: What happens if you call `resultSet.previous()` on a default JDBC `ResultSet` created by `conn.prepareStatement(sql)`?
options: Moves cursor cleanly back one row
Throws `SQLException` because default `ResultSet` is `TYPE_FORWARD_ONLY`
Returns `false` silently and stays on the current row
Re-executes the SQL query from row 1
questions.explanation: By default JDBC creates `ResultSet.TYPE_FORWARD_ONLY`; calling `previous()`, `absolute()`, or `first()` throws a `SQLException` unless `TYPE_SCROLL_INSENSITIVE` / `TYPE_SCROLL_SENSITIVE` is requested.

questions.question: A loan form accepts ages `18` to `65` inclusive. Selecting test inputs `{17, 18, 19, 64, 65, 66}` exemplifies which QA testing technique?
options: Statement Coverage
Boundary Value Analysis (BVA)
Mutation Testing
Regression Fuzzing
questions.explanation: Testing `min-1, min, min+1, max-1, max, max+1` targets off-by-one boundary defects, the essence of Boundary Value Analysis.

questions.question: What does the following Java code print?
options: HCL
HCLTech
Other
OtherTech
questions.explanation: Java passes object references by value. `sb.append("Tech")` mutates the shared object on the heap (`HCLTech`), while reassigning the local parameter `sb = new StringBuilder(...)` only changes the local copy of the reference, leaving `s` pointing to `HCLTech`.

questions.question: Given `Sales(sale_date, amount)` with unique dates, which SQL expression computes the cumulative running total up to each row's `sale_date`?
options: `SUM(amount) OVER ()`
`SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)`
`SUM(amount) GROUP BY sale_date`
`ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY sale_date)`
questions.explanation: Specifying `ORDER BY sale_date` with frame `ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` sums all rows from the start of the partition through the current row.

questions.question: A directed graph admits a valid topological ordering if and only if it is:
options: Bipartite
Complete
A Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)
Strongly Connected
questions.explanation: Any directed cycle makes `u before v` and `v before u` mutually impossible; every finite DAG has at least one topological sort (found via Kahn's algorithm or DFS finish times).

questions.question: How is an ARP Request sent on an Ethernet LAN, and how does the target host reply?
options: Request is unicast; Reply is broadcast
Request is Layer-2 broadcast (`FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF`); Reply is Layer-2 unicast
Both Request and Reply are multicast across the WAN
ARP runs over UDP port 53
questions.explanation: Because the sender does not yet know the target's MAC address, the ARP Request is broadcast across the local LAN segment; the matching target replies directly via unicast using the sender's MAC.

questions.question: What happens at the CPU hardware level when a user-space program invokes `read()` on a file?
options: The CPU remains in User Mode and reads disk sectors directly
A software interrupt / `syscall` trap switches the CPU from User Mode (ring 3) to Kernel Mode (ring 0) to execute the OS handler safely
The JVM Garbage Collector suspends all kernel threads
The MMU disables virtual memory translation permanently
questions.explanation: Protected hardware I/O cannot run in unprivileged user mode; `syscall`/`int 0x80` traps into kernel mode, validates permissions/buffers, performs I/O, and returns to user mode.

questions.question: Which restriction applies to a Java `record` (e.g., `record Point(int x, int y) {}`)?
options: A record cannot implement interfaces
A record is implicitly `final` and cannot extend another class (other than `java.lang.Record`)
A record cannot declare static methods or compact constructors
Record fields are mutable by default via generated setters
questions.explanation: Java `record`s are shallowly immutable data carriers: all components are `private final`, the record class itself is implicitly `final` (cannot extend classes), though it CAN implement interfaces and define custom constructors/methods.
